lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Fractions and Decimals
lesson.summary: Equivalent fractions, comparing, fractions of amounts, adding fractions, tenths and hundredths, money and percentages.
learning_objectives: Find equivalent fractions and compare them

standards.text: Recognise and show equivalent fractions; add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Recognise and write decimal equivalents of tenths, hundredths and quarters

success_criteria: I can find a fraction of a number
I can write tenths and hundredths as decimals and use money
lesson.real_life: Sharing a pizza, shop sales with percent off, and paying in pounds or rupees.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how are fractions, decimals and percentages all connected?
blocks.say: Welcome back, number explorer! Imagine one pizza cut into eight slices. You eat two slices. Your sister eats two slices. Did you eat the same amount as someone who ate one quarter? Fractions help us share fairly. Decimals and percentages are fraction cousins, and shops use them every day. Today we will explore all three. Let's go!

terms.meaning: Three ways to write parts of a whole.

blocks.markdown:
**Equivalent fractions** are the same amount with different names.

1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8
blocks.say: Here is a chocolate bar. If we cut it into two equal pieces and take one, we have one half. Now cut each half in two. We have four pieces, and two of them are shaded. Two quarters. The shaded part has not changed at all. It is the same amount with a different name. We say one half and two quarters are equivalent fractions. Cut again into eight, and four eighths is the same too.

blocks.title: One half, two quarters, four eighths

scenes.caption: 1/2 shaded
scenes.say: One half. The bar is in two equal parts and one is shaded.

scenes.caption: 2/4 shaded = 1/2
scenes.say: Cut each half in two. Now two out of four are shaded: two quarters. The same amount!

scenes.caption: 4/8 shaded = 1/2
scenes.say: Cut again. Four out of eight are shaded. Four eighths. Still the same amount.

question.explanation: 2 out of 4 equal parts is the same as 1 out of 2.

blocks.markdown: Multiply the top (**numerator**) and the bottom (**denominator**) by the same number: 1/3 = 2/6.
blocks.say: Here is the trick. Multiply the top number and the bottom number by the same number, and the fraction keeps its value. One over three, times two on top and bottom, is two over six.

blocks.title: One third = two sixths
blocks.caption: 2 of 6 parts shaded is the same as 1 of 3.

question.hint: What was 5 multiplied by to get the new bottom?

blocks.markdown: The bigger the denominator, the smaller each piece. 2/3 is bigger than 2/5.
blocks.say: To compare fractions, look at the size of the pieces. Two thirds and two fifths both have two pieces. But thirds are bigger pieces than fifths, because the whole is cut into fewer parts. So two thirds is bigger than two fifths. The bigger the bottom number, the smaller each piece.

scenes.say: Two thirds. The bar has three parts and two are shaded.

scenes.caption: 2/5 is less than 2/3
scenes.say: Two fifths. The bar has five parts and two are shaded. The shaded part is shorter.

question.explanation: Fourths are bigger pieces than eighths, so 3/4 is bigger than 3/8.

blocks.say: Remember. Equivalent fractions are the same amount. Multiply top and bottom by the same number. The bigger the bottom number, the smaller the pieces.

sub_lessons.title: Fractions of amounts and adding fractions

blocks.text: Stop 1: Finding a fraction of a number

blocks.markdown:
To find a fraction of an amount: **divide** by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.

1/4 of 20 = 5 and 3/4 of 20 = 15.
blocks.say: What is one quarter of twenty? Share twenty into four equal groups. Each group has five. So one quarter of twenty is five. What about three quarters? Three groups of five make fifteen. The bottom number tells us how many groups to share into. The top number tells us how many groups to take.

scenes.say: Share them into four equal groups. Each group has five stars.

scenes.caption: 3/4 of 20 = 15
scenes.say: Take three of the four groups. Three times five is fifteen. So three quarters of twenty is fifteen.

blocks.title: Fractions of 20
blocks.goal: Put the stars into 4 equal boxes. How many in one box? That is 1/4 of 20.
blocks.say: Now try it with your hands. There are twenty stars. Share them into the boxes to find a fraction.

blocks.markdown: Same denominator? **Add** the numerators. The denominator stays the same: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.
blocks.say: When the bottom numbers are the same, adding is easy. Two sevenths plus three sevenths. The pieces are the same size, so we just add the tops: five sevenths. The bottom number stays the same. It only tells us the size of the pieces.

scenes.say: Add three more sevenths. Now five of the seven parts are shaded.

question.hint: Add the tops. Keep the bottom.

points: Fraction of an amount: divide by the bottom, multiply by the top
blocks.say: Remember. For a fraction of an amount, divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top. To add with the same bottom, add the tops.

terms.meaning: Put together to make a total.

blocks.markdown: A **decimal** is a fraction written with a **decimal point**. 1/10 = 0.1 and 3/10 = 0.3.
blocks.say: A decimal is another way to write a fraction. Cut one whole into ten equal parts. Each part is one tenth. We write one tenth as nought point one. Three tenths is nought point three. The dot is called the decimal point. It sits between the whole numbers and the parts.

blocks.title: Tenths from 0 to 1
blocks.caption: Ten equal steps from 0 to 1. Each step is one tenth, 0.1.

question.hint: Tenths go straight after the decimal point.

blocks.markdown: **Hundredths** are two places after the decimal point. 1/100 = 0.01 and 25/100 = 0.25 = 1/4.
blocks.say: Now cut each tenth into ten more pieces. Now the whole is cut into one hundred equal parts. Each tiny part is one hundredth, nought point nought one. Twenty-five hundredths is nought point two five. And that is exactly one quarter!

scenes.say: Cut it into ten tenths. Three tenths are shaded: nought point three.
Each tenth cut in ten makes a hundred. Twenty-five of them make nought point two five, which is one quarter.

blocks.title: Fraction pairs
blocks.say: A little brain break. Find the matching pairs.

question.prompt: 0.5 is the same as one half.

blocks.say: Remember. Tenths are the first place after the decimal point. Hundredths are the second place. Nought point five is a half and nought point two five is a quarter.

terms.meaning: A number with a decimal point, like 0.3.
The dot between whole numbers and parts.
Ten equal parts of one whole.
One hundred equal parts of one whole.

mini_quiz.prompt: Match the fraction to the decimal.

blocks.markdown:
Money is a decimal: £4.60 means 4 pounds and 60 pence.

Line up the decimal points when you add.
blocks.say: Money uses decimals every day. Four pounds sixty is written four point six zero. The digits after the point are the pence. A pound is one hundred pence, so every pence is a hundredth. When we add money, line up the decimal points. Four pounds sixty plus two pounds seventy-five is seven pounds thirty-five.

question.hint: Add the pence, then the pounds.

blocks.say: A percentage is a fraction out of one hundred. The word percent means per hundred. Fifty percent means fifty out of a hundred, and that is one half. Twenty-five percent is a quarter. Ten percent is one tenth. Shops use percentages for sales.

scenes.say: Here is a hundred square. Fifty squares are shaded: fifty percent. That is one half.
Twenty-five squares shaded is twenty-five percent. That is one quarter.
Ten squares shaded is ten percent. That is one tenth.
